answer.rationale: Rollback (memory_b1) is off the table: compliance has ruled the security patch non-revertible, so the single strongest historical precedent is unavailable regardless of how well it worked on day 18. The signal that actually discriminates here is that the degradation is confined to the primary region while the release went to all regions two hours ago — a region-scoped symptom points at a region-scoped cause (host/storage/replication-layer contention in the primary) more than at the new build, though I cannot rule out the build interacting with primary-region-only state. That makes regional_failover the best-matched intervention, and memory_b2 is the closest analogue, so I want its original record to check what the March degradation actually was, whether writes were at peak, and whether replication lag was measured during the shift — the consolidated summary says 'traffic shifted cleanly' but a failover under heavy settlement writes can drop or duplicate in-flight writes, which directly violates the 'without losing customer writes' constraint. I also want memory_b5, because it is the only serious alternative: offloading report reads reduced primary contention and recovered write latency same-day, which is exactly our symptom class and is far lower-risk than moving regions during peak. If the b5 record shows the contention profile matched (dashboard/report reads crowding the write path), I would switch to route_read_replicas as the safer first move. add_capacity (memory_b3) is a pre-provisioning success, not an in-incident lever — 90 minutes into a climb it will not land in time. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) fails fast on an external dependency; here the write path is ours and shedding writes at settlement peak sacrifices the exact thing we are protecting. I am therefore committing to a small_guarded_test: shift a bounded slice of write traffic out of the primary with replication lag and write-acknowledgement as explicit abort gates, rather than a broad cutover, because the inherited memories record outcomes without recording the conditions that made those outcomes safe, and a broad failover at peak is the one move whose failure mode is unrecoverable customer write loss.
